items.title: Canada's Weston Family Agrees $8.9bn Boots Deal, Marking Return To Ireland
items.summary: Canada's Weston has entered into an agreement to acquire Boots and its associated businesses for $8.9 billion (€7.96 billion).

items.title: Xandres is growing in the Netherlands and expanding into Germany
items.summary: Xandres attributes its revenue growth in the past fiscal year primarily to strong momentum in the Netherlands. Now, the Belgian fashion company is shifting its focus to Germany. Its ambition remains to grow into a strong European brand.

items.title: PepsiCo Running Out Of Time To Meet Elliott-Inspired Targets As GLP-1 Threat Intensifies
items.summary: PepsiCo is running out of time to deliver on the growth and margin targets set out after Elliott took a $4 billion stake last year.

items.title: Coca-Cola steps into better-for-you soda market with prebiotics
items.summary: The soda giant is entering the buzzy category and will compete with Olipop and PepsiCo-owned Poppi.

items.title: UK's Imperial Brands Affirms Annual Outlook, Launches $2bn Share Buyback
items.summary: Imperial Brands said on Thursday it was on track to meet its full-year guidance and launched a new £1.5 billion (€1.8 billion) share buyback.

items.title: Danone-Backed Biotechnology Platform Opens Industrial Facility
items.summary: Danone-backed Biotech Open Platform has inaugurated a new biotechnology platform in Clermont-Ferrand, France.

items.title: Danish Crown To Focus On Europe, Announces Organisational Changes
items.summary: Danish Crown plans to introduce a new organisational structure, while Finn Klostermann will step down as Danish Crown Beef CEO.

items.title: Europe allocates 3.8 million euros for laid-off Cora employees in Belgium
items.summary: More than 1,000 former Cora employees in Belgium are receiving additional support in their job search. The European Parliament is allocating 3.82 million euros for this purpose. By the end of September, 34% of the former employees receiving support had already found a new job.

items.title: EIT Food-Backed Startup Raises €15m To Scale Microalgae Protein
items.summary: French startup Edonia has raised €15 million to scale the production of a whole-food protein ingredient derived from microalgae.

items.title: Nestlé Shoots To Score Younger Generation With NBA Deal
items.summary: Nestlé is making its biggest-ever international sponsorship play through an NBA deal with its cocoa and malt drinks business.

items.title: Ghirardelli brings 174-year-old chocolate brand to packaged cookies
items.summary: The baked good will be pitted against other premium offerings in the $2 billion cookie space, such as Mondelēz’s Tate’s.

items.title: Constellation Brands acquires spirits RTD brand SpikedAde
items.summary: Constellation Brands has bought US RTD brand SpikedAde in a deal that could be worth up to $353m.

items.title: Lacoste fires its CEO
items.summary: Lacoste dismissed CEO Éric Vallat last week, just before the fashion show during Paris Fashion Week. Thierry Guibert is once again taking the helm at the French luxury lifestyle brand.

items.title: Izy Coffee restarts with 11 coffee bars following a “quiet bankruptcy”
items.summary: Izy Coffee is making a fresh start with eleven coffee bars. To do so, the Belgian chain is utilizing the new procedure for confidential bankruptcy preparations. Five locations will close, but 85% of the employees will keep their jobs.

items.title: British drugstore chain Boots to come under Canadian ownership
items.summary: The Canadian billionaire Weston family, former owners of the luxury department store chain Selfridges, is acquiring the British drugstore chain Boots from the investment fund Sycamore Partners. This brings an end to several months of uncertainty.

items.title: Back To Basics - Thor Skov Jørgensen On Coop Danmark's Turnaround Strategy
items.summary: The CEO of Coop Danmark, Thor Skov Jørgensen, tells Rose Costello how the organisation has been progressing with its turnaround strategy.

items.title: Nestlé signs largest-ever brand partnership with the NBA
items.summary: Nestlé is partnering its Milo, Nescau, and Nesquik brands with the NBA worldwide. Starting in 2027, the multi-year agreement will cover 21 markets on four continents, marking the largest international brand partnership in the group’s history.

items.title: “We wanted to rocket fuel our growth” – Borough Broth CEO Ros Heathcote on funding, GLP-1s and AI
items.summary: Borough Broth founder and CEO Ros Heathcote chats with Just Food on the plans ahead, the protein trend and operational challenges The post “We wanted to rocket fuel our growth” – Borough Broth CEO Ros Heathcote on funding, GLP-1s and AI appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: High costs are causing concern at PepsiCo
items.summary: Despite a better-than-expected third quarter, PepsiCo is lowering its full-year guidance due to persistently weak demand for snacks and beverages in North America and sharply rising costs.

items.title: Uniqlo’s parent company, Fast Retailing, surprises with fifth consecutive increase in profits
items.summary: Fast Retailing closed its fiscal year with its fifth consecutive record profit. The owner of Uniqlo attributes this to strong performance across all regions, despite pressure from the weak yen in its home market.

items.title: Müller plans to close two factories in Germany
items.summary: Theo Müller plans to close two production plants in eastern Germany – one manufacturing sauces and another cheese. The post Müller plans to close two factories in Germany appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Heaven Hill sells liqueur brand Irish Mist
items.summary: US spirits group Heaven Hill Brands has offloaded liqueur brand Irish Mist to Ireland-based The Old Canal Quay Spirits Company.

items.title: Russia Dominates Sunflower Oil Shipments, Pushing Ukraine Out Of Big Markets, UAC Union Says
items.summary: Russia is pushing Ukraine out of core markets by undercutting it on price and leading to a slowdown in Ukrainian shipments, UAC Union said.

items.title: Pilgrim’s Europe Reports Profit Rise In FY25 Driven By Strategic Investments
items.summary: Pilgrim’s Europe has reported positive results in its 2025 financial year, driven by strategic investments and growth in poultry.

items.title: Cinnamon roll chain Have A Roll sets its sights on Wallonia
items.summary: In mid-November, Have A Roll will open a new store at the Woluwe Shopping Center. It will be the company’s eighth location in Belgium and its second in Brussels. The chain plans to expand into Wallonia soon.

items.title: Belgian princess Delphine’s art reproductions remain on Aldi shelves
items.summary: Aldi's art campaign featuring Princess Delphine does not appear to be repeating the success of the one with Koen Vanmechelen—at least for now. More than a week after its launch, the reproductions are still in ample supply at some stores.

items.title: Colombia’s coffee crop survives earthquake but El Niño looms
items.summary: For Colombia’s coffee industry, El Niño-related risks are expected to have a far greater impact on production than the August earthquake.

items.title: ASOS confirms that hackers breached the app for a ransom note
items.summary: ASOS confirms that hackers exploited the fashion retailer’s app for a public extortion attempt, a rare tactic in cyberattacks. The online clothing retailer says basic data may have been accessed, but sees no impact on payment card information or passwords at this time.

items.title: B&G Foods pulls Nortera deal amid regulator backlash
items.summary: B&G Foods has pulled the sale of its Green Giant and Le Sieur vegetable businesses in Canada to Nortera Foods due to regulatory opposition. The post B&G Foods pulls Nortera deal amid regulator backlash appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Street food fuels rise of South Korean cuisine
items.summary: For brands and retailers, South Korean foods are no longer a niche proposition but a platform for growth. The post Street food fuels rise of South Korean cuisine appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Treasury Wine Estates cuts 170 jobs in push for “simpler” organisation
items.summary: Treasury Wine Estates has laid off more than a hundred jobs across the Australian wine giant's global "corporate functions".

items.title: Vion eyes Dutch slaughterhouse sale
items.summary: Vion plans to sell one of its pig slaughterhouses in the Dutch group's domestic market due to declining volumes. The post Vion eyes Dutch slaughterhouse sale appeared first on Just Food .

items.title: Albertsons Appoints Cody Perdue As Interim CFO
items.summary: US food and pharmacy retailer Albertsons Companies has named Cody Perdue as its interim chief financial officer.

items.title: Japan’s anti-trust watchdog raids four major brewers in price cartel probe
items.summary: Japan's antitrust body has searched the offices of four local brewing giants over allegations that they breached the country's competition law.

items.title: Modelo maker buys boozy sports drink SpikedAde for $75M
items.summary: The beer maker is broadening its portfolio with the vodka and sports drink brand as it looks to tap into growing demand for RTDs.

items.title: Tesco Raises Profit Outlook Floor After First-Half Rise
items.summary: Tesco lifted the bottom end of its full-year profit outlook after reporting a 6.5% increase for its first half.

items.title: Apps, AI Among Essentials In Marketing Strategies For German Retailers – EHI
items.summary: Retailers’ apps and the use of AI remain key aspects in marketing strategies, as per a recent study from the EHI Retail Institute.

items.title: Online is a key growth driver for Tesco
items.summary: Tesco, the largest British supermarket chain, has reported strong results for the first six months of its fiscal year. Growing online sales are driving growth at the retailer, which plans to increase its focus on AI.

items.title: From Belgian chocolate to Belgian fashion: Broeklin unveils new tenants
items.summary: Broeklin Brussels announces its first tenants. Following Celio, Neuhaus, Xandres, and Jimmyz Burgers have now also confirmed they will be joining the shopping project in Machelen. Meanwhile, construction has begun.

items.title: German Retail Association Voices Concern Over Plans For National Plastic Tax
items.summary: The German Retail Association (HDE) has voiced concern over the government’s plan to introduce a national plastic tax.

items.title: What barriers and opportunities face functional beverage makers?
items.summary: Industry executives at the Non-Alcoholic Beverages conference delved into issues such as the need to clarify benefits in functional drinks.
